name: Margaret Rose
heroAlt: Margaret Rose standing in a rose garden in warm evening light
tributeHtml:
Her kindness was her legacy.
Her love lives on.
shareDescription: A personal memorial song created from her story.
lyrics:
She loved the soil upon her hands
And sunlight in her hair
She grew roses in her garden
And left her kindness there

She knew the names of every child
Who passed her classroom door
And somehow made the quiet ones
Believe a little more

She kept a tin of buttons
And letters tied with string
Birthday cards from years gone by
And every precious thing

Margaret Rose, we’re missing you
And all the love you gave
In gardens full of morning sun
In every heart you shaped
You gave us words, you gave us grace
You taught us how to care
And when the roses bloom again
We’ll feel you standing there

She made a home where tea was poured
And cake was always near
Where every guest was welcomed in
With “come on in, my dear”
She loved the spring and Sunday roast
The books beside her bed
The stories read to bright young eyes
The little prayers she said

And though we wish for one more cup
One more “come in, my dear”
The love she gave so freely
Is still living with us here

Margaret Rose, we’re missing you
And all the love you gave
In gardens full of morning sun
In every heart you shaped
You gave us words, you gave us grace
You taught us how to care
And when the roses bloom again
We’ll feel you standing there

So rest now, gentle Margaret
Your work on earth is done
The seeds you planted long ago
Are reaching for the sun
rememberingParagraphs: Margaret was a much-loved wife, mother, grandmother, teacher and friend whose kindness shaped both her family life and the many classrooms she cared for.
She shared more than fifty years with her husband, David, and was a devoted mother to Helen and Thomas. Later, Sophie, Ben and Emily brought her the deep joy of becoming a grandmother.

For over three decades at St Anne’s Primary School, Margaret was known for noticing the quiet child, remembering every birthday and helping each pupil feel that they mattered. At home, the same warmth lived in her garden, her books, her Sunday roasts and the open invitation to come in for tea.
storyParagraphs: Margaret Rose was born in Kent in 1946, the second of three sisters. She grew up in a busy family home where clothes were mended, letters were saved and the garden was treated almost like another room. Her mother taught her how to take cuttings and her father encouraged her love of reading, two interests that stayed with her throughout her life.

She met David at a local summer dance when they were both in their early twenties. He was drawn to her quiet humour, while Margaret liked his steadiness and the way he always made sure everyone got home safely. They married in 1971 and built a life together that would span more than fifty years.

Their daughter, Helen, arrived first, followed three years later by their son, Thomas. Margaret created a home where routines mattered but laughter was never far away. Sunday lunch, birthday cakes, school shoes by the radiator and books read aloud at bedtime became part of the family rhythm.

Margaret trained as a primary school teacher and spent more than thirty years at St Anne’s Primary School. She especially loved teaching younger children and had a gift for noticing those who were shy, anxious or easily overlooked. Former pupils remembered her calm voice, her neat handwriting and the way she made them believe they could do more than they thought.

When Helen and Thomas grew up and had families of their own, Margaret embraced being a grandmother to Sophie, Ben and Emily. She kept drawings on the fridge, saved every handmade card and always had a book or small garden job ready for their visits. Her grandchildren came to know that her home was a place where time slowed down and they were always listened to.

Her garden became even more important after retirement. Roses lined the path, sweet peas climbed by the fence and herbs grew close to the kitchen door. Margaret joined the local gardening club, swapped cuttings with neighbours and quietly delivered flowers to anyone who was ill, grieving or simply in need of cheering up.

She remained a loyal friend and an attentive neighbour. Tea was poured generously, cake was usually nearby and nobody was hurried away. Margaret remembered anniversaries, asked after people’s children and kept letters, buttons, photographs and small objects because she understood how ordinary things become precious when they carry a memory.

Margaret’s life was not loud, but it was rich with care. David, Helen, Thomas, Sophie, Ben and Emily remember the steadiness she brought to family life, while generations of pupils remember the confidence she placed in them. Like the roses she tended, the kindness she gave continues to bloom in the lives she touched.
